jobs.title: Sr. Strategic Project Engineer-Packaging
jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 40590

Cheers to creating an incredible tomorrow!

At Molson Coors, we tackle big challenges and defy the status quo. With a proud legacy of excellence, an incredible portfolio of beer, seltzers, spirits, and non-alcohol brands, and a bold vision for our future... we're on the path to transforming the beverage industry. That requires remarkable individuals who are curious, tenacious, and never afraid to fail forward.

We seek, value and respect everyone’s unique perspectives and experiences knowing that we are stronger together. We collaborate as a team and celebrate each other’s successes.

Here’s to crafting careers and creating new legacies.

The Crafted Highlights

In the role of Sr. Strategic Project Engineer – Packaging in Milwaukee, WI, you will lead the development of long-range capital strategies for packaging and warehouse investments across North America. You will also lead front end project development, including business case analysis, alternative development and evaluation, concept development, and preliminary capital budgeting to ensure investments are technically sound, financially justified, and aligned with long-term business objectives.

Reporting to the Sr. Director, Capital Planning, Packaging, Controls & Warehouse Execution, you will serve as a recognized subject matter expert for major Integrated Supply Chain initiatives.

What You'll Be Brewing

• Lead the development of strategic capital initiatives across Packaging and Warehouse operations.

• Develop and support 3-year and 10-year capital strategies.

• Identify and develop capital improvement opportunities that reduce COGS across Packaging and Warehouse operations, including labor, maintenance, waste and line/equipment efficiency

• Establish scope, schedules, budgets, risk assessments, and business cases.

• Evaluate breakthrough programs, technologies, and process improvements.

• Provide technical leadership and packaging expertise.

• Assess emerging technologies and manufacturing approaches.

Key Ingredients

• You have 15+ years of relevant experience in capital project development, packaging engineering, manufacturing, supply chain operations, or the beverage industry.

• You possess a Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or a related technical discipline.

• A Master's Degree or Postgraduate Degree is preferred.

• Experience developing large-scale strategic capital projects.

• Deep expertise in high-speed packaging systems, warehouse operations, industrial automation, and beverage manufacturing processes.

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

• You build relationships and collaborate to achieve desired outcomes.

• You act with integrity and accountability while driving results.

• You have a thirst for learning and are always looking for ways to learn and help others grow.

Beverage Bonuses

• Flexible work programs that support work-life balance including a hybrid work model of 4 days in the office.

• We care about our People and Planet and have challenged ourselves with stretch goals around our key priorities.

• We care about our communities and play our part to make a difference.

• Engagement with Employee Resource Groups.

• Ability to grow and develop your career centered around First Choice Learning opportunities.

• Participation in our Total Rewards program.

• On site Pub, access to brand clothing and swag, top events and free beer and beverages!

• Work within a fast-paced and innovative company.

Molson Coors is an equal opportunity employer. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, veteran status or any other characteristic. If you have a disability and believe you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or recruitment processes, please e-mail jobs@molsoncoors.com .

Pay and Benefits:

At Molson Coors, we’re committed to paying people fairly and equitably for the work they do.

Job Posting Total Rewards Offerings : $129,900.00 - $170,500.00 (posting salary range) + 20 % target short term incentive + $12,500 + 400 Non-Qualified Stock Options target long term incentive + $23,000 on average spent on benefits per employee, including but not limited to health, dental, vision, retirement with above market employer match, wellness incentives and EAP + paid time off (including holidays, vacation days and sick days).

The posting range provided above for salary is what we, in good faith, believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We ultimately pay based on a number of non-discriminatory factors that inform pay decisions including but not limited to the required work location, previous work experience, skill set and internal equity.

jobs.title: Packaging Engineer II, Amazon Leo
jobs.description:
LEO is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

The LEO team is looking for an exceptional Packaging Engineer to join our team and drive standardization and efficiency for product packaging in our supply chain. The Packaging Engineer will work closely with Engineering, Global Commodity Management, Supplier Quality Management, and Operations teams in the US and abroad to define efficient, robust, and standardized packaging for our products. You will be a critical escalation path for packaging issues and work closely with partner teams to ensure cross-functional collaboration is effective.

The team is looking for knowledge in the following fields of focus:
- Clean room compliant packaging
- Manufacturing kit packaging
- Manufacturing shadow form solutions
- Transportation solutions
- Labeling and barcoding (including developing supplier standards for labeling/barcoding)
- Proven strong organizational and problem-solving skills
- Demonstrated critical thinking capability
- Enthusiasm for getting “hands on” with your team in collaborative environments
- Ability to identify risks, develop clear mitigation plans, and communicate effectively to executive stakeholders while handling multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced rapidly evolving environment

Key job responsibilities
- Partner with operations to identify packaging/labeling defects impacting operations, including safety hazards created by packaging.
- Manage the development of Packaging concepts with Packaging Vendors and Component part Suppliers, ensuring material conformity and personnel safety.
- Plan and direct activities concerned with design and development of packaging. Analyze engineering drawings and specifications of product to determine physical characteristics of component, special handling and safety requirements.
- Create detailed packaging specifications for both components and manufacturing kits, including clean room compliance.
- Define standard labeling and barcoding specifications and partner with supply chain to drive adoption by suppliers. Monitor adherence to standards and drive corrective actions as appropriate.
- Scope new technology and/or opportunities in the packaging space.

jobs.title: System Development Engineer, Robotics Delivery & Packaging Innovation (RDPI), RDPI Hardware Solutions
jobs.description:
Robotics Delivery & Packaging Innovation (RDPI) Global Engineering is looking for a System Development Engineer (SysDE) to join our New Product Introduction (NPI) team. Our mission is to eliminate operational complexity at the source, ensuring every RDPI automation solution is designed for deployability, reliability, and maintainability from Day One.

As a SysDE II on the NPI team, you will work alongside Hardware Development programs from the Alpha phase to help shape controls and system design before solutions are built. Rather than fixing deployment and reliability problems in the field, you will help design them out — contributing to the automation, firmware, and integration decisions that determine how easily a solution scales across our global network. You are a builder who designs and delivers the controls software and tooling for the systems you support, works autonomously on well-scoped problems while seeking direction on ambiguous ones, and partners with Hardware Development, Technical Program Managers, and the Scale and AI teams to deliver solutions that deploy with minimal human intervention.

This role is a strong fit for an engineer who thinks software-first and wants to grow in the software development craft. You will deepen core software engineering practices — modern languages, testing, CI/CD, and AI-native, agentic development — and apply them to industrial controls and hardware domains.

Key job responsibilities
- Contribute to NPI programs from Alpha through GA, helping influence controls and system design for deployability, reliability, and maintainability.
- Design and deliver standardized hardware/software interfaces and modular, reusable control patterns that reduce integration complexity, with guidance on the most ambiguous architectural decisions.
- Build and validate automation and commissioning frameworks (CI/CD for controls code, automated configuration validation, emulators) in partnership with the Scale team.
- Participate in reviews of architecture, design, and operations for your solutions, and incorporate feedback to raise the quality of your work.
- Partner with Hardware Development, TPMs, and the AI team to incorporate self-service deployment and predictive capabilities into solutions.
- Use AI-assisted and agentic development tools to increase the quality and velocity of your engineering work, and share what you learn with the team.
- Apply and help improve engineering and operational excellence standards, and mentor interns and junior engineers as you grow.

A day in the life
You work across industrial control platforms (Codesys, Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Beckhoff) and the networked field devices, firmware, and cloud/WMS interfaces around them. You design and build the controls software for a solution, contribute reusable control patterns to our libraries, write and review structured-text and automation-tooling code, and work with Hardware to improve a system before it's built. You take part in design reviews that surface architectural and scalability risks early, and you prototype frameworks, emulators, automated validation, and CI/CD for controls code that become the foundation future solutions are built on. You lean on AI and agentic development tools throughout — generating, testing, and troubleshooting code — so you can focus your judgment on building solutions that are correct by design.

jobs.title: Packaging Lead Engineer
jobs.description:
Packaging Lead Engineer

In this role you will be responsible for setting up the enterprise packaging strategy and technology roadmap while leading a group of engineers.

Develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive process standards and documentation to support all end-to-end packaging business and engineering workflows.

Establish packaging standards and lead execution of automation, returnable, and expendable plans while setting the standard on how Autoliv will achieve cost, quality, and sustainability goals. Assign workload to a team of engineers for new launch.

Should you be interested in overseeing these tasks and aiming for enhanced performance standards, your role will involve :

What you'll do

• Establish and maintain packaging standards for automation, returnable, and expendable execution; publish controlled specifications and playbooks

• Lead governance for exceptions/waivers; chair the standards review board and manage change control (ECO/ECN)

• Define common footprints and automation execution standards; align with safety/quality and sustainability requirements.

• Own enterprise packaging data architecture and tools (spec/PFEP, cartonization, labeling, image vaults): governance, permissions, and data-quality SLAs.

• Standardize master data (part-to-pack links, dunnage IDs, test results, sustainability attributes) and audit routines; lead training and adoption.

• Select/administer cartonization and labeling systems (GS1/AIAG compliant), including template libraries and formal change control.

• Set/enforce ID standards (serialization, barcode/QR/RFID), labeling, and traceability checkpoints (ship/receive scans, gate checks).

• Own the portfolio/roadmap for packaging materials, formats, and automation; prioritize pilots with success criteria and scale proven solutions.

• Conduct market/technology scouting; partner with suppliers/startups to mature innovations into standards.

• Develop KPIs/dashboards; monitor compliance and drive corrective actions with site leaders.

• Mentor regional teams; build capability via training, playbooks, and office hours

• Lead and set workload for a team of packaging engineers for new model launch and serialization projects

What is required

• BS in Packaging Engineering (preferred) or ME/IE

• 7–10+ years in packaging or logistics engineering, including multi-site standards/systems ownership in automotive/Tier-1 or similar high-volume manufacturing.

• Hands-on with PFEP/spec databases, cartonization (TOPS/Cape or WMS-native), labeling, and GS1/AIAG compliance.

• Experience integrating packaging data with ERP/PLM/WMS (e.g., SAP/Oracle; Teamcenter/Windchill); strong Excel/BI; familiarity with APIs/MDM concepts.

• Working knowledge of ISTA/ASTM transit testing, load-securement, and sustainability/EPR considerations.

• CAD & Packaging: SolidWorks/NX/CATIA; ArtiosCAD for corrugated/dunnage; read drawings, GD&T, basic tolerance stacks.

What’s in it for you

• Attractive compensation package

• Recognition awards, company events, family events, university discount options and many more perks.

• Gender Pay Equality

Equal opportunity employer

Autoliv is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Autoliv does not discriminate in any aspect of employment based on race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, gender, sexual orientation, gender identify and/or expression, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local employment discrimination laws where Autoliv does business.
